solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In general, nowhere is safe ultimately at sea

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word safe
being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A warning that, for someone on a ship, no place is ever truly secure in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' shuffles NOWHERE IS plus E, the last letter of 'safe' picked by 'ultimately'. 'In' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was a US Army five-star general before becoming President.

clue.text: Stylish mature wife's left clique

parts.note: in means fashionable or stylish

indicators.note: the wife has left, so that letter departs from the word for maturing

parts.note: to mature is to grow up
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A fashionable grown woman has walked out on her circle of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes W from GROWUP, leaving GROUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is an exclusive circle of insiders, the same as a closed social group of this kind.

clue.text: In most of the night in Paris? That's tedious

definitions.note: the definition names a state that is tedious: weary boredom

parts.note: en is French for in, the 'in Paris' applying to this word too

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter, here the T is dropped

parts.note: nuit is French for night

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a stay in Paris spent mostly at night is really so dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' makes both 'In' and 'the night' French: EN and NUIT, with 'most of' cutting NUIT to NUI.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, borrowed from French, names listless boredom, which is what a tedious thing produces.

clue.text: Drugged girl caught in charge of antiseptic

indicators.note: caught as in heard or overheard, so the girl's description is taken by ear

parts.note: drugged is high, and the girl is Jean, giving 'high Jean'

explanation.surface: A girl who has been drugged is found in the custody of something sterile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' signals a sound-alike: 'high Jean' sounds like the start of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiseptic means free of germs, clean and sanitary, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Distraught WI's hang-up: £51 for cleaner?

indicators.note: distraught means very upset, so the letters of the Women's Institute's hang-up are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters W, I, S, H, A, N, G, U, P
51 is LI in Roman numerals and £ is a quid, giving LI and QUID

explanation.surface: The Women's Institute is upset about its obsession over paying fifty-one pounds for a cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation; a quid is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: This detergent for dishes is a cleaner, a substance that cleans.

clue.text: It's very hard to get collar right at the front

indicators.note: one letter for right is moved to the very front of the word

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: Getting a criminal into custody is extremely difficult when you are positioned on the right side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link; 'right at the front' moves one R of ARREST to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of rare: something hardest of all to come by or obtain.

clue.text: Forward at Twickenham barges in there

definitions.meaning: a second-row forward in rugby union; Twickenham is England's national rugby ground in London
a canal chamber where barges are raised or lowered between water levels

explanation.surface: A rugby player at Twickenham shoves his way into a ruck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barges in' looks like pushing rudely; here barges are canal boats.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a rugby position in the scrum and a canal chamber with gates.

clue.text: Steward left with a bloke

parts.note: and means together with
a gent, short for gentleman, is a man or bloke

explanation.surface: A steward walked out, accompanied by some fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward manages an estate on the owner's behalf, the role of an estate manager.

clue.text: Funny bug coated in black stuff

indicators.note: the bug is covered by the black stuff, sitting inside it

parts.note: coal is black fuel
a bug is a hidden microphone, a mic

explanation.surface: An amusing insect has been smeared with something dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like an insect but is a listening device.
explanation.definitionFit: Comical means amusing or laughable, the same as funny.

clue.text: It's not for out-of-court battle

indicators.note: out of means without, so the word court is taken away from the battle

parts.note: Agincourt was Henry V's 1415 victory over the French
taken as written

explanation.surface: A refusal to support settling a dispute without going to court.
explanation.walkthrough: Dialect AGIN means against, i.e. not for.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect form of against, describing a position opposed rather than in favour.

clue.text: Cook should study this golf course

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
astronomy is a course one might study at university

explanation.surface: A chef ought to look into this particular golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Cook also studied the stars; 'Cook' here is a chef.
explanation.definitionFit: The art and science of good food and cooking is what a chef studies.

clue.text: Basque queen once forfeited acres

indicators.note: losing or giving up the acres means those letters are taken out

parts.note: Boadicea was the ancient British queen of the Iceni
A stands for acre, so acres are two As

explanation.surface: A queen from the Basque country once lost her land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basque' looks like a nationality but is a close-fitting garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A basque is a tight-fitting woman's top, a kind of laced corset-like garment for the torso.

clue.text: Fashionable attitude, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable
a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: Being trendy is an outlook, for one, someone says.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case or example, as in 'for instance'.

clue.text: Jump over a rope at first, doing this in gym

indicators.note: the jump goes over, that is around, what follows

parts.note: to spring is to jump

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of rope

explanation.surface: Instructions for leaping across a skipping rope to start a gym workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The gym is a boxing gym, where practice bouts are fought.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers practise with a partner in a gym, going through practice bouts.

clue.text: Golfer hires pro, eliminating error in skill set

indicators.note: the golfer hires, taking on staff, so holds the next piece inside

parts.note: Rory McIlroy, the Northern Irish golfer

indicators.note: eliminating means removing the cross from the word for a pro

parts.note: a pro is an expert
an X is the cross that marks an error

explanation.surface: A golfer takes on a coach to cut mistakes out of his game.
explanation.walkthrough: Rory McIlroy is a Northern Irish golfer; an error is marked with a cross, X, which 'eliminating' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertory is the stock of pieces or abilities one can draw on, a repertoire.

clue.text: South African driver absorbs large amounts of material

indicators.note: the golfer takes in the letter, which goes inside his name

parts.note: Ernie Els, the South African golfer, who drives the ball

explanation.surface: A motorist from South Africa soaks up great quantities of stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist, but it is a golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old measure of cloth length, so several of them are quantities of fabric.

clue.text: Wearing suit? Emphatically so

definitions.meaning: holding spades, the card suit, as though dressed in it

explanation.surface: Is he in a suit? Very much so.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in large amounts, very much; spades are also a suit of cards.

clue.text: Turkey's force cut

definitions.note: the definition is 'Turkey' plus 's, meaning a turkey is

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force
to lop is to cut

explanation.surface: The Turkish military's strength has been reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the country, but means a failure; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is a show or product that fails badly, a complete failure.

clue.text: Bedridden chap lacking iron receives help

indicators.note: the remainder takes in the help, holding it inside
lacking means without, so the iron symbol is taken off the chap

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
aid is help

explanation.surface: A man confined to bed, short of iron in his blood, gets some assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking iron' removes FE from FELLOW, leaving LLOW to hold AID.
explanation.definitionFit: To be brought down by illness and confined to bed, the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Painting I replaced with one of Renoir's in flat

indicators.note: the letter I is swapped out and the French one put in

parts.note: a painting is a picture
un is French for one, as the French painter Renoir would say

explanation.surface: An art buyer swaps a canvas for one of Renoir's works for display in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but means a burst tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat tyre results from a hole in it, so a flat is a burst or punctured tyre.

clue.text: Badminton prize does restrict allotted time

indicators.note: the deer hold the other pieces within them

parts.note: roe deer; does are female deer
set means fixed or allotted

explanation.surface: Female deer limit how long one may play for a badminton trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton is a famous English horse trials event, not the racket sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is the ribbon award given to placed horses and riders at the event.

clue.text: Big stone pieces in this spot, so I'm told

indicators.note: so I'm told means as heard, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: chess pieces are men, and in this spot is here: men here

explanation.surface: Someone reports that giant pieces of rock are located at this site.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall upright standing stone of prehistoric times is a big stone set on end.

clue.text: PM's edited diaries about Peel finally

definitions.note: the definition is 'PM' plus 's, meaning a prime minister is

indicators.note: the rearranged diaries go around the next letter
edited suggests the diaries have been reworked into a new order
finally takes the closing letter of Peel

explanation.surface: A prime minister's revised journals concerning Robert Peel, another prime minister, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' reworks DIARIES into DISRAEI, and 'about' wraps it round the L from 'Peel finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British prime minister, as was Peel.

clue.text: Finish investing last of 5 in Victoria

indicators.note: investing means clothing or wrapping, so the name goes around the piece

parts.note: Victoria Beckham was Posh Spice
the closing part of 5-down's clue is '£51', which supplied LI there

explanation.surface: A cleaning tip: complete the job by putting the last of the 5-down detergent into Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse of LI is uncertain: 51 is LI in Roman numerals, from the '£51' at the end of 5-down's clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish is a glossy finish or refinement given to a surface.

clue.text: Some spell in Gordonstoun, some can't

definitions.note: read as 'some cant': a form of slang or jargon

indicators.note: some of the words, that is, part of their letters, run together inside them

explanation.surface: Some pupils at Gordonstoun, a Scottish boarding school, can spell and others cannot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the apostrophe: 'can't' is cant, jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is jargon or slang, a variety of cant.

clue.text: Holmes to initiate subject of one of his cases

parts.note: to blood a novice is to initiate them

parts.words: subject of one of his cases
parts.note: the Hound of the Baskervilles is a famous Sherlock Holmes case

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes is about to begin investigating one of his mysteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes is a relentless tracker, a figurative sniffer dog of detection.

clue.text: Crazy students flood West End

indicators.note: the students pour around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: the NUS is Britain's National Union of Students

indicators.note: End takes the final letter of West

explanation.surface: Mad students pour into London's West End theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nuts is slang for mad or insane.

clue.text: State curbs Welsh leader's power

indicators.note: curbs means restrains, so the verb holds the letter within

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: the leader of Welsh is its first letter

explanation.surface: The government restrains the authority of the head of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold sway is to have power or influence over others.

clue.text: Turn up again in middle of street party extremely cut

indicators.note: middle of takes the central pair of letters in street

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: A street party is badly cut short, but people show up for it once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of VERY, giving VER.
explanation.definitionFit: To rediscover is to find again, to turn something up a second time.
